'''Will Herthie Shields''' (born September 15, 1971) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 14 seasons.  He played [[college football]] for the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska Cornhuskers]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors and winning the [[Outland Trophy]]. Shields played his entire, 14-year professional career with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] and never missed a game. Shields was selected to 12 [[Pro Bowl]]s, was a three-time First-Team [[All-Pro]], a four-time Second-Team All-Pro, and was selected to the [[National Football League 2000s All-Decade Team|NFL 2000s All-Decade Team]]. He won the [[Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award|Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year]] award in the 2003 season, was inducted into the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 2011, and was inducted into the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 2015.

Bartee missed the entire [[2006 Kansas City Chiefs season|2006 season]] due to injury and was placed on the [[Physically Unable to Perform|PUP]] list in November. He was released by the Chiefs after the season.
